images.prompt: Orthographic side view (left half of the canvas) and front view (right half) of the same creature: Khasar, an enormous ancient cave wolf-beast, a four-legged wolf the size of a horse-drawn cart, NOT a werewolf, never standing upright. Long low body, very heavy deep-chested forequarters and massive shoulders, the head carried low below the shoulder line, slimmer tucked hindquarters, long thick tail held low. A thick shaggy black-grey hackle mane from the skull to the middle of the back, with a few jagged dull grey stone shards grown into the mane over the shoulders like crystals in old rock. Soot-grey fur in layered tones, pale dusty underbelly, old scars: the left ear torn with a notch, pale scar lines across the muzzle, a bald scar on the flank. Around the neck the remains of a broken collar of old yellowed bone plates on a cracked leather cord, half of it missing. Heavy wide paws with dark worn claws. Small dim ember-orange eyes, deep-set, not glowing. Mongolian steppe wolf proportions (long legs, deep chest) exaggerated into an ancient cave predator.

Three-quarter front view of Khasar, an enormous ancient cave wolf-beast, crouched low in a dark limestone cave mouth, snarling with the scarred muzzle wrinkled and long yellowed fangs bared. Four-legged wolf anatomy, NOT a werewolf: massive shoulders, deep chest, head low and forward, thick black hackle mane bristling with a few grey stone shards grown into it, torn left ear, pale scar lines across the muzzle, a broken bone-plate collar on a cracked leather cord around the neck. Soot-grey layered fur, paler dusty underside, heavy paws with dark claws. Small dim ember-orange eyes. A faint cold breath vapour from the mouth. Ancient, patient and dangerous, an old predator of the steppe that has lived in the cave for centuries.
